content: Individuals diagnosed with diabetes are at a significantly higher risk of developing sensory impairments, including hearing loss. Research indicates that the prevalence of hearing loss in people with diabetes is approximately twice as high as in those without the condition. The underlying mechanisms proposed to explain this association include microangiopathy, which involves damage to small blood vessels, and auditory neuropathy, which refers to dysfunction in the auditory nerve. Both of these mechanisms are thought to result from chronic hyperglycemia and oxidative stress, which are common complications of diabetes. Furthermore, diabetes has also been associated with impairments in the senses of taste and smell in certain cases, although these occurrences may vary among individuals.
